cards.explanation: The answer is the ends of the earth. The verse says, “…His praise from the ends of the earth…” (Isaiah 42:10). Friends, the call goes way past one building. It reaches right out to the far edge of the map.

The answer is True, and the sea gets a front-row seat. The verse says, “…you who go down to the sea, and all that is in it, you islands, and all who dwell in them.” Sailors and island folks are both on the invite list. Nobody is too far out to sing.

The answer is the mountaintops. The verse says, “Let the people of Sela sing for joy; let them cry out from the mountaintops.” Sela is a city in Edom (2 Kings 14:7). A mountaintop is a spot where your voice carries.

The answer is that He roars in triumph. Verse 13 says, “He shouts; yes, He roars in triumph over His enemies…” The LORD isn't tiptoeing in here, friends. He goes forth like a mighty one, and the roar is a victory roar.

The answer is a woman in labor. God says, “But now I will groan like a woman in labor; I will at once gasp and pant.” After ages of quiet, the sound changes. This is a God who has held back and is now about to act.
The answer is False. God says, “I will turn the rivers into dry land and drain the marshes.” No flood in this verse, friends. The rivers become dry land, and the marshes are drained (Isaiah 42:15).

The answers are light and level. God says, “I will turn darkness into light before them…” (Isaiah 42:16). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and the light is a very big deal to me. Then the verse says, “…and rough places into level ground.” The bumpy road gets smoothed out for the ones He's guiding, and a smooth path beats a bumpy one every time.

The answer is False. Right after the promise to lead, God says, “These things I will do for them, and I will not forsake them.” (Isaiah 42:16). He doesn't drop them halfway, friends. That's a promise I'd want to hear in the dark.

The answer is turned back in utter shame. God says those who trust in idols and say to molten images, ‘You are our gods!’ “will be turned back in utter shame.” That's how it ends for them, according to God.

The answer is His own servant. That's the twist, friends. God asks, “Who is blind but My servant, or deaf like the messenger I am sending?” He's pointing at His own servant, and I did not see that coming.
The answer is True. God asks, “Who is blind like My covenant partner, or blind like the servant of the LORD?” He says it in a few ways, so you can't miss it. The same people keep getting named.
The answer is hear. God says, “Though seeing many things, you do not keep watch. Though your ears are open, you do not hear.” The ears are open, friends, but the hearing isn't happening.

The answer is that He was pleased to magnify His law and make it glorious. Verse 21 says, “The LORD was pleased, for the sake of His righteousness, to magnify His law and make it glorious.” He lifts it up. That's what pleased Him.

The answer is False, and it's a hard verse. They “…have become plunder with no one to rescue them, and loot with no one to say…” the words “Send them back!” Nobody speaks up for them here, friends. I think that's the heaviest part.
The answer is obey. The passage asks, “Who among you will pay attention to this? Who will listen and obey hereafter?” Hearing is the first step, friends, and obeying comes with it.

The answer is the LORD, and it's a hard one. The passage asks, “Who gave Jacob up for spoil, and Israel to the plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned?” The way the question is put points straight to the LORD.

The answer is that they would not walk in His ways. The verse says, “They were unwilling to walk in His ways, and they would not obey His law.” The reason comes right after the question, friends. It's a hard one to hear, but it's plain.

The answer is False, and it's a sobering one. The text says, “…but they did not understand; it consumed them, but they did not take it to heart.” They didn't understand, and they didn't take it to heart. And the story isn't over, friends, because the book of Isaiah keeps going.
